camp.about: Work crews pitch their tents where the day's digging ends. The cook hangs a pot by the path so a latecomer can find supper without waking a tentful of sleepers.

well.about: A ring of fitted stones keeps loose earth out of the spring. The rim has a low shelf where a child can rest a full jar before lifting it.

quay_steps.about: Porters use the lowest dry step to board a boat. As the tide rises they move their baskets up the stone stair, one landing at a time.

workshop.about: Boatwrights steam planks over a trench of hot stones, then bend them round wooden pegs. A split plank still makes a pair of good oar blades.

market.about: Growers bring fruit down in leaf-lined baskets. The jars go home full of salt fish, packed for villages too far inland to smell the sea.

gateway.about: The sun mosaic belongs to everyone on market mornings. Fishers spread their catch around its rim and leave the centre clear for the porters with their baskets.

lodge.about: Boat crews share sleeping mats here between tides. The keeper saves the places nearest the door for those who must put out before dawn.

archive.about: A keeper presses each household's seal into wet clay beside its account. Even a borrower who cannot read can find her own mark and call for witnesses.

observatory.about: Watchers sight the rising stars between pairs of stone uprights. The first dawn appearance of the rainy season's star gives farmers time to bring their grain under cover.

fountain.about: Clay pipes bring spring water to the jade basin. The lip is cut low on one side so a small child can dip a cup while the tall jars fill.

temple.about: Households bring a little of their first flour to the sun court. The temple ovens bake it into small loaves for people who have come to town with nothing to offer.

log_cabin.about: Trappers hang wet hides under the eaves and stretch them on willow hoops. A traveller who finds the cabin empty may sleep by the hearth and leave a split log for the next guest.

apothecary.about: The herbalist dries leaves on reed trays and keeps the roots in separate clay pots. A sprig tied to each lid tells an apprentice which plant grew it.

mess_hall.about: Crews bring their own bowls to the long tables. One cook can feed a whole shift while the hearth is hot and have the grain soaking for the next.

stilt_house.about: Timber posts carry the sleeping floor above the flood line. A family can tie its boat to the steps and come home even when the lane is under water.

map_room.about: Pilots bring the cartographer depths knotted into sounding cords. A shoal earns its place on the harbour chart when a second boat finds it.

greenhouse.about: Tender seedlings spend their first weeks under cover. The gardener opens the shelter early, before the midday heat can wilt a whole bed.

trading_post.about: Masons dress one face of each block at the quarry. At the post a buyer lays two faces together. Daylight in the joint means more work before the stones can go on the cart.

water_mill.about: Water turns a paddle wheel geared to the upper millstone. A miller tests the meal between finger and thumb. A fine loaf calls for a narrower gap between the stones.

clock_tower.about: The harbour watch cuts a mark on the staff at each highest tide. Pilots consult the marks before they risk a deep-laden boat over the bar.

lighthouse.about: The keepers haul baskets of dry wood to the brazier before dusk. Out at sea a pilot steers towards the fire until the harbour mouth opens between the reefs.

treehouse.about: Fruit pickers keep a sleeping platform among the branches. A watcher with a rattle can turn a flock away before it strips the ripest tree.

aviary.about: Boat crews take birds from this loft to sea in wicker cages. Released with a slip of linen round one leg, a bird can bring word home before the rowers make land.

beached_ship.about: Shipwrights draw the pegs from a stranded hull at low tide. Curved ribs are worth saving whole. A young boatbuilder might wait a season to find a tree bent to the same shape.

amphitheater.about: On contest days the wrestlers oil their shoulders under the lowest tier. On hearing days a petitioner stands on the same patch of sand and the whole town can hear.

museum.about: Families lend the hall things too dear to sell. On feast days a player may lift a harp from its peg so the children hear the instrument their grandparents danced to.

hanging_gardens.about: Each terrace drains into the bed below. Gardeners carry water to the top at dawn and plant the thirstiest herbs where the first runnel falls.
